items.anchor: For delayed interception, reset elapsed time at the pursuer's start. If target position relative to the start is D+Vs+As²/2, constant pursuer speed required for contact is D/s+V+As/2 for s>0. An unrestricted minimum for D,A>0 occurs at s=√(2D/A), but a finite time window may exclude it. Compare required speeds over the actual domain; endpoint contact can be optimal. Worked anchor: D=9 m, V=1 m/s, A=2 m/s² gives required speed 1+s+9/s, minimum 7 m/s at s=3 s when allowed; with a 2 s window the smallest speed is 7.5 m/s at closure. Check the interval before interpreting a double root.
items.novelty: Delayed release plus disjoint observation windows; separate endpoint minima and compare them globally; unrestricted tangency excluded.
items.shortest_author_route: Build both positions on the delayed clock; derive f(s); prove monotonic direction separately on each allowed window, compare endpoint minima, and test the changed connected domain.

Keep each velocity regime and its time domain. Worked anchor: L=40 m, A starts at 0 with +3 m/s, B at 10 with −1 m/s. Relative coordinate −10+4t reaches 0 at 2.5 s and 40 at 12.5 s. If a direction switch occurs, carry the relative coordinate continuously to the switch and search multiples separately. A first positive contact may occur at k≠0.

items.transfer_w: Execute the prescribed signed constant-acceleration equations for two different launch magnitudes and a shared depth; eliminate depth and check physical event times.
items.anchor: For two projectiles launched from one height with the same constant g, choose one downward-positive axis and use H=u_i t_i+gt_i²/2 for each. Equal depth is an equation, not permission to equate launch speeds. Worked anchor: one starts at rest, reaches a lower sensor at 3 s with g=8 m/s², so H=36 m. Another launched upward at 5 m/s reaches that depth when −5t+4t²=36; retain the positive root and check it follows the turn. The shortcut u=g(t₂−t₁)/2 holds only for equal opposite magnitudes.

items.transfer_w: Execute a specified equal-distance reciprocal-time relation with dwell and moving-only time, reject physically invalid current roots and verify both leg times.
items.anchor: For equal out-and-return distances d at constant water-relative speed v and current c, the ground speeds are v+c and v−c. A return requires 0≤c<v. Moving time is d/(v+c)+d/(v−c)=2dv/(v²−c²); elapsed time includes any dwell. Worked anchor: d=120 m, v=4 m/s, c=2 m/s gives moving times 20 s and 60 s, total 80 s. A 10 s wait makes 90 s elapsed; average speed is 240/90, not (6+2)/2. To infer c from a clock, subtract dwell first and reject nonreal or domain-invalid results. This is a current/relative-velocity model, not a general law of wind-driven boats.
items.shortest_author_route: Build the two leg time ledger plus dwell, solve the reciprocal equation in the physical domain, and substitute both leg times into the original clock. Check the minimum elapsed time at zero current.
